**Finding submitted: deviation (rule IP).**

- **Where:** § 7.0 Materials (p0082–p0086). Deliverables default to **Type II Materials** — IBM or third parties hold all right, title and interest, and we get only a licence to use/reproduce/distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only," with no right to modify or sublicense (and "Enterprise" is limited to US entities).
- **Why it fails:** Preferred (we own work product created for us) is not met, and the fallback is also missed because the licence-back lacks modification and sublicensing rights and is territorially/entity-restricted.
- **Customer Data:** No assignment of our data to IBM (Content/Customer Components are defined as ours; IBM gets only Required Consents), but there is no express ownership statement — added for certainty, plus a no-joint-ownership sentence.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** flip the default to **Type I Materials** and insert a new § 7(e) confirming our ownership of Content/Customer Components and Type I Materials. Type I already grants IBM a broad licence back, so IBM retains use of its own know-how; fallback offered in the comment (keep Type II default if the licence is expanded to perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense).
